articles.title: Janmashtami Special: CM Yogi Adityanath to Offer Prayers at Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura
articles.description: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will visit Mathura on Janmashtami to offer prayers and perform darshan at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple as the city celebrates the birth anniversary of Lord Krishna. Mathura and Vrindavan are witnessing elaborate religious programmes, temple decorations and a large gathering of devotees for the festival. Ahead of his visit, CM Yogi highlighted the changing atmosphere in Uttar Pradesh, saying that while disturbances were witnessed before 2017, the state is now celebrating its cultural and religious heritage. The Chief Minister’s Mathura visit comes amid heightened preparations for the Krishna Janmotsav, with devotees arriving from different parts of the country to participate in prayers and celebrations. Special rituals, aartis and devotional programmes are being organised at temples across the region, while security and crowd-management arrangements have also been strengthened. The midnight moment marking Lord Krishna’s birth remains the central highlight of the celebrations, with devotees observing fasts and waiting for the ceremonial prayers. Mathura, regarded as Krishna’s birthplace, holds special significance during Janmashtami, drawing thousands of pilgrims and visitors. CM Yogi’s visit is expected to add political and administrative focus to the festival, while the government continues to promote Uttar Pradesh’s religious heritage and major pilgrimage destinations. The celebrations across Mathura and other parts of the state reflect the strong cultural significance of Janmashtami, with temples illuminated, devotional music filling the streets and devotees participating in traditional festivities.
